event.summary: Ordinary-create placement stacking is preserved; spawn intentionally fixes its host
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435. TLDR: Rechecked the original concern that a recipe template followed by an ordinary-host template would fail despite a valid final host; both the classification path and its ordinary-create fallback preserve that valid stack. Details: create_for_agent 1991–2008 calls plan_environment_create only for fleet-origin, hostless, non-spawn creates naming a recipe template. plan_environment_create 4229–4254 loads recipes/places and uses resolve_placed; a final host target yields None. resolve_agent_create 2447–2480 then loads recipes/places again and calls resolve_placed, so it does not lose the earlier valid recipe template. Explicit --host is carried as host_given, and agent_launch.rs 215–219 clears every template placement before application. This matches SPEC.md 4143–4149: 'Templates are applied first, in order' and 'an explicit flag wins over a template'. Spawn uses agent_launch::resolve at agent_requests.rs 2437–2445 with empty recipes/places (agent_launch.rs 147–150) and host_fixed=true (233–238). It does not inherit the ordinary-create stacking allowance: SPEC.md 4148–4149 states, 'farhelm spawn targets its own host, so a template that sets a host is refused there.' The shared apply_template enforces host_fixed before availability checks for both host fields (launcher.rs 913–919) and recipe targets (940–947), and apply_templates 987–998 stops at the first refused template. Thus an earlier placement template cannot be hidden by a later template on spawn. For ordinary creates, each intermediate template must still be individually applicable: launcher.rs 948–958 validates recipe/place, 970–978 validates home-folder placement, and 987–998 stops at the first refusal. The final-placement rule is not a promise to skip invalid earlier templates. The direct helper test at agent_launch.rs 478–536 covers both valid placement orders and explicit --host; the caller checks establish the integration premise absent from that test. event.detail: Reviewed commit: 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435. TLDR: The new fake environment supervisor used to check copied launch commands treats an ordinary Farhelm heartbeat as malformed JSON and panics. If the test's connected fixture lives through its first heartbeat, it can lose the peer needed for its create observation for a reason unrelated to launch preservation. This is a maintainer fixture-protocol defect, not a production heartbeat failure or an observed flake. Details: the assigned new spawn_launch_recording_responder reads each frame at agent_requests.rs 15378 then unconditionally calls parse_control(&frame).expect at 15384 before matching CreateSession. FrameReader::read_frame returns decoded frames without filtering kind/body (proto/io.rs 166–170), and parse_control directly JSON-decodes frame.body at 249–250. The manager enables heartbeat for every environment host, including the planted Podman host in this test, at manager.rs 4275–4280. SupervisorClient maps that boolean to a 30-second period at client.rs 1814–1831; its independent writer timer starts at now+period (1948–1952) and emits Frame::data(0, Vec::new()) on the tick (1955–1964), regardless of request/cache traffic. The splice consumes SetBrowserForwarding and ListSessions only (rest_harness.rs 610–645), then forwards this empty Data frame verbatim at 646. Empty bytes are not JSON, so the valid heartbeat reaches the expect panic. The test an_environment_clone_keeps_a_launch_todays_catalog_would_refuse starts this responder at 15447–15448, connects it as a session-owned Podman environment at 15453–15459, waits through a real handler/card and Deny at 15464–15492, then needs the same responder for the real create entry point at 15497–15512. There is no fixture-wide below-30-second lifetime guarantee; the card wait alone is bounded at twenty seconds, while setup/database/create phases are separate awaits. The standard runner permits multiple sixty-second periods (.config/nextest.toml 19–21), so its outer deadline does not exclude the heartbeat. Normal quick runs may finish before it. The panic is in a detached task, and the splice intentionally keeps the manager side alive after peer exit (rest_harness.rs 588–603), so the precise later visible symptom depends on which phase remains; no symptom or frequency was executed or measured.
